An elementary derivative test proves the unique crossing; stochastic row sums and W_i>=D prove the sharp induced norm envelope and singleton equality. Taylor/limit arguments are explicit. evidence: The convex-filter theorem proves positivity assuming global convexity and f(nh)<=1. The new semigroup can have negative cross-clique entries; therefore the convexity hypothesis is violated and its positivity conclusion cannot imply the new negative phase.

The complete-multipartite theorem gives positivity recovery and peak norms for a different family, intersecting the present family at stars; this overlaps but cannot imply the all-heterogeneous-clique-cone norm extremizer.
The Gauss-Legendre windmill result studies a rational polynomial quotient and non-heat sign transition; it is not an exponential semigroup theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new result is neither a rewording of convex-filter positivity nor a corollary of the restricted complete-multipartite family. The known spectral projector identities are a common premise, and the novelty is explicitly confined to the nonconvex semigroup phase and topology-optimal norm statement. A stronger unlocated full-semigroup theorem could still subsume it.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison of exact hypotheses and quantifiers: earlier spectral decompositions and the 2026 convex-filter entry formulas are credited; the new theorem treats all increasing (often nonconvex exponential) generators, sharp continuous-time positivity recovery, and an attained topology-wide norm extremizer. Star cases were already covered and are not independent novelty. Historical-priority risk from unindexed literature remains.
residual_risks: Shared exact projector entry formulas from the convex-filter theorem make the new semigroup classification an accessible extension; the value rests on an all-generator structural classification and topology extremality, not on rediscovering the formulas.
Not all older functional-calculus and eventual-positive matrix papers were accessible in full or exhaustively searched.
The original 2019 fractional-network preprint was checked at abstract level only; a related 2021 full-text treatment of the same framework was read.

value.rationale: Natural complete phase classification for a broad non-Bernstein family of clique-cone graph semigroups, with an exact topology-invariant restoration time and a sharp worst-case transient norm over all community decompositions of fixed size. This couples two-spectrum reduction with network robustness extremality; it is not merely a single numerical slice or a star special case.
